title: Release anchor + peg scratchpad
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick personal scratchpad for an anchor+peg rollout pattern I want to try next week for v2.3.0 (tokenization fix + kv-cache change).
- Objective: deploy without user-visible regressions, keep median latency within 10% of baseline, cap token cost delta < 8%.
- Constraints: small burstable pool in us-west1 for dedicated customers, hosted API traffic across two regions.

Terminology (working):
- anchor: a stable, pinned image (v2.2.9) that serves as the fallback and baseline for comparison.
- peg cohort: small, short-lived cohorts that are switched between anchor and candidate to probe differences while maintaining session affinity.
- drift window: short observation window (3–10 minutes) used for early signal detection.

High-level plan (staggered anchor+peg):
1) Preflight (30–60m before rollout window): warmup anchor instances (ensure KV priming), confirm load tests pass on candidate in staging identical to prod config.
2) Canary-peg phase (first 60m): create 4 peg cohorts (0.05%, 0.1%, 0.25%, 0.5%). Each cohort will alternate between anchor and candidate every 10 minutes in a staggered sequence (anchor->candidate->anchor) so the same client IDs see both within a short time.
3) Evaluation slices: after each peg cycle, run automated diff checks on metrics and small eval set (10k prompts sampled from recent traffic).
4) Ramp: if no red flags at 0.5% peg, slowly shift steady-state traffic 5% -> 20% using large cohorts while keeping an anchor baseline receiving 10% traffic.
5) Full promote or revert depending on quality and infra signals.

Why this pattern?
- Alternation reduces cohort-level bias (time-of-day/segment).
- Having an anchored baseline in production reduces blast radius: we always have a known-good route.
- Short peg cycles give signal quickly without long-lived user impact.

Quick checklist (preflight):
- [ ] Confirm infra has dedicated warmup capacity (SRE check-in).
- [ ] Create feature flags + routing policy in console for peg cohorts (names: peg-A..peg-D).
- [ ] Update rollout runbook with immediate pin command and contact list.
- [ ] Smoke test latency p50/p95 and correctness on a small test query set (local).
- [ ] Ensure eval harness (evals/realtime) is pointed at traffic mirror and can run within 10m.
- [ ] Notify SRE, Oncall, and CS (30m before).

Safety signals and thresholds (working numbers):
- Latency: p95 candidate > anchor_p95 * 1.25 -> HOLD and investigate.
- Errors: 5xx or model timeouts absolute increase > 0.5% AND relative increase > 2x baseline -> ROLLBACK to anchor.
- Quality: prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE-style eval drop > 3% on tracked prompt set -> FLAG for triage.
- Cost: tokens/sec increase > 12% sustained over 15m -> pause ramp and inspect.
- Anomaly score: model-output hash drift > threshold (too many changed tokens in top-1) -> pause.

Monitoring quick-queries (Prometheus/Grafana examples):
- sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~".*candidate.*"}[5m])) by (le) vs anchor.
- increase(redwood_inference_errors_total{status=~"5..",route=~".*candidate.*"}[10m]) / increase(redwood_inference_requests_total{route=~".*candidate.*"}[10m])
- custom eval job: POST /internal/eval/run with body {sample_set: "recent-10k", model: "candidate"} -> returns quality delta.

Operational commands (cheat sheet):
- Pin traffic to anchor (immediate):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $RLW_TOKEN" \ 
    https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/routing/pin \ 
    -d '{"route":"/generate","target":"anchor-v2.2.9","reason":"rollback immediate"}'
- Switch cohort routing: console CLI (local): rwctl route set --cohort peg-B --target candidate-v2.3.0
- Emergency full-swap: rwctl route replace --route /generate --target anchor-v2.2.9 --force --note "emergency rollback"

Peg sequencing (example timeline, 60m):
- 00:00–10:00 -> peg-A anchor, peg-B anchor, peg-C candidate, peg-D anchor
- 10:00–20:00 -> rotate one step so each cohort sees candidate in different windows
- Repeat for 3 full rotations (30m) then evaluate

Client affinity notes:
- Session pin TTL: keep short (5–10m) for pegs so users see both versions, set cookie-based client-id mapping when available.
- For long-lived sessions (desktop apps), avoid including them in early pegs. Mark them as "anchor-only" until steady state.

Evaluation hooks:
- After each rotation, auto-run micro-evals: grammar checks, hallucination detector, top-k token distribution diff. If any micro-eval returns > threshold fail rate, suspend candidate.
- Post-deploy (24h): full eval against 100k production-sampled prompts and human QA on edge cases.

Escape hatches and postmortem triggers:
- Immediate: pin all traffic to anchor (command above) + page SRE (pager duty runbook).
- Deferred: if quality regressions persist > 4 hours, schedule rollback to previous deploy and create incident with Sev2.
- Postmortem: attach eval diffs, a timeline of cohort swaps, and hot traces from candidate instances.

Open questions / TODOs (my notes):
- Need a simple label in telemetry that ties a request -> peg-cycle id (so we can diff within same minute). Add an ephemeral header X-Peg-ID.
- Are we okay alternating client IDs that affect downstream caching? Might confuse caches. Talk to infra team about cache partitioning.
- How to safely exclude logged-in internal users? Add allowlist in routing policy.
- Investigate short-lived priming traffic to kick KV caches on candidate before each peg window. Might reduce cold-start noise.

Notes for post-run analysis (what I'll pull):
- sample of 5k request traces grouped by peg id, with tokens generated and top-3 logits where possible.
- delta table: latency, errors, cost per 1k tokens, quality score per prompt bucket (length bins).
- config snapshot: runtime flags, quantization profile, compiler kernels used.

Rationale for thresholds: mostly conservative given recent regression that only appeared at p95 and in cost metrics. We want to protect latency-sensitive interactive users but still surface small correctness regressions quickly.

Quick contact list (who to page):
- Oncall SRE: Nico Alvarez
- Serving runtime lead: Priya Sharma
- Product owner: Daniel Cho (for customer impact decisions)
- Eng support (CS point): Maya Thomson

Final quick notes to self:
- Keep the first peg cycles short and noisy; real signal accumulates across alternations not just one window.
- Avoid big cohorts until we have consistent pass across 3 alternations.
- Document any manual intervention timestamped in the runbook (important for postmortem).

-- end scratchpad --
